trip.title: Forest of Dean · 26–30 Oct
trip.description: Dog-friendly walks, food and towns near Forest Holidays Forest of Dean, 26–30 October 2026.

origin.name: the cabin
origin.address: Forest Holidays Forest of Dean, Bracelands Drive, Coleford GL16 7NN

trip.checkLabel: Ring ahead: dog policy not confirmed

areas.title: On your doorstep (0–5 mi)
areas.note: Coleford, Staunton, Symonds Yat and Clearwell, all within about 10 minutes.

areas.title: Central forest (4–9 mi)
areas.note: Beechenhurst, Cannop, Speech House, Parkend and Mallards Pike, a few minutes from each other.

areas.title: Monmouth (5 mi west)
areas.note: 10 minutes from Staunton and Symonds Yat.

areas.title: Ross-on-Wye and Goodrich (7–15 mi north)
areas.note: Goodrich and Kerne Bridge are on the way to Ross; Symonds Yat is 15 minutes from Ross.

areas.title: Lower Wye Valley (11–16 mi south)
areas.note: Tintern, Wyndcliff and Chepstow, each 5–10 minutes apart.

areas.title: Lydney and the Severn side (9–14 mi south-east)
areas.note: The railway, Taurus Crafts and the harbour are all around Lydney.

areas.title: Further afield (25 min+)
areas.note: Only if you fancy a longer drive.

areas.title: Essentials
areas.note: Vets, food shopping and medical help.

places.note: Woodland tracks straight from the cabins. An easy first walk to let the dog settle in.
A dog- and child-friendly pub with a beer garden. You can walk there, so nobody has to drive.
Country pub. Visit Dean Wye pairs it with a ~5 mi Joyford walk.
Small market town for supplies, the Forest Deli and the Dog House micropub (very dog-friendly but small).
A short, steep climb to a huge rock with views into Wales. You can carry on through Highmeadow Woods for longer.
places.near: Next to the White Horse; 10 min to Monmouth

walk.length: Short; longer loops through Highmeadow Woods

places.note: A country pub that welcomes walkers, families and dogs, and has its own host dog. Visit Dean Wye pairs it with an ~8 mi Staunton walk.
A famous viewpoint over a loop of the River Wye. The path from the car park to the viewpoint is short and easy. There's parking, toilets and bins.
places.near: Start of the Biblins loop; 1 mi above the Saracens Head

places.note: About 4.5 mi from Symonds Yat Rock, down to the river and over the Biblins suspension footbridge. Steep at both ends, so use the carriers. Take the bridge rather than the hand-pulled ferry.

places.n: The Saracens Head, Symonds Yat East
places.q: Saracens Head Inn, Symonds Yat East
places.note: A riverside gastro-pub. Dogs are allowed in the bar and outside. Visit Dean Wye pairs it with a 5 or 7 mi River Wye walk. The road down is narrow and steep.
A small steam railway with woodland play trails. Listed as dog-friendly. Check the half-term timetable.
places.near: Just south of Coleford; 5 min from Clearwell Caves

places.note: Old iron mines with a café and shop. Dogs are welcome on the surface but not in the caves, so take turns. Booking online is recommended.
places.near: Next to Tudor Farmhouse; 5 min from Perrygrove

places.note: A smarter restaurant with rooms. Listed as dog-friendly. Good for a treat night.
places.near: In Clearwell village, by the caves

places.note: A traditional old pub, listed as "dogs welcome". It may be snug, so ask for a quiet spot. Opening hours vary by day.
About 3.5 mi on wide gravel paths past big sculptures. Easy to shorten. There's parking, toilets and bins.
places.near: Café on site; 1 mi to Cannop Ponds and Speech House

places.note: Refurbished, open every day. Dogs sit in "the snug", a quieter separate area. Serves soups, burgers and sharing plates.
Flat paths around two ponds with ducks. Parking, toilets and bins.
places.near: Next to the Cycle Centre café; 1 mi from Beechenhurst

places.n: Forest of Dean Cycle Centre Café
places.q: Pedalabikeaway Forest of Dean Cycle Centre
places.note: Dog-friendly. Sandwiches, soups, and vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options.
A big country hotel with two restaurants and heated outdoor dining dens. The best roomy, calm pick for a nervous dog. Also serves morning coffee and afternoon tea.
Newer café with indoor and outdoor seating, water bowls and dog biscuits. Toasties, paninis and cake.

places.q: New Fancy View, Forest of Dean
places.note: A viewpoint on an old colliery tip with a short walk up. A good quick stop.
places.near: On the way to Mallards Pike

walk.length: Short walk up to the viewpoint

places.q: Mallards Pike Lake, Forest of Dean
places.note: An easy 1.5 mi lake loop with a lakeside café that has water bowls and dog treats (roughly 10am–4pm). Parking, toilets and bins.

places.n: Soudley Ponds and Dean Heritage Centre
places.note: A pretty walk round a chain of woodland ponds, next to the local museum and café. Check whether dogs are allowed inside the centre.
An easy town to wander: the 13th-century Monnow Bridge with its gatehouse, Agincourt Square, Church Street's shops and the riverside.
places.near: 10 min from the Buckstone and Symonds Yat

places.q: The Punch House, Agincourt Square, Monmouth
places.note: Recently voted Wales' most dog-friendly pub. Pub food made with Welsh ingredients.
A coffee shop with a big outdoor area at the back and a menu for dogs. It can get busy at the counter.
Brunch and tapas. Dogs allowed inside and out, with water bowls and treats.
A National Trust hilltop with the Round House and big views over Monmouth. There's a short walk from the car park, or a steep climb up from town.

walk.length: Short from the top car park, or a steep climb from town

places.note: A red sandstone castle run by English Heritage. Its listing says dogs are accepted; check which areas.
places.near: Just up the hill from Kerne Bridge and the Inn on the Wye

places.n: Inn on the Wye, Kerne Bridge
places.q: Inn on the Wye, Kerne Bridge
places.note: A traditional pub-restaurant, dog- and family-friendly. Dogs are welcome in the restaurant and bar, and it's a larger venue.
places.near: Below Goodrich Castle; 10 min to Ross

places.note: The most dog-friendly town around. Over 30 shops, 14 pubs and a dozen cafés have joined the "We Welcome Dogs" scheme, so look for the purple stickers. See the Market House and the Prospect gardens over the river.
By the river, fully dog-friendly, with a wood burner.
A big terrace and gardens overlooking the Wye. Likely roomy inside too.
A deli with a secret courtyard garden at the back. Quiet, so good for a nervous dog.

places.q: Thorns Coffee Lounge, Croft Court, Ross-on-Wye
places.note: Plenty of space on the outdoor terrace.

places.q: Victorias Coffee Shop, Broad Street, Ross-on-Wye
places.note: Dog-friendly, known for its cakes and savoury bakes.
A friendly café where dogs are more than welcome.
Listed as dog-friendly for lunch or dinner. A riverside spot just over the bridge from Ross.
A country pub listed as dog- and child-friendly, with good food.
Cross the old railway bridge and climb Offa's Dyke Path to a rock viewpoint over the abbey. About 5 mi there and back, and steep. Use the carriers.
places.near: Starts at Tintern; 10 min to Chepstow

places.note: Dramatic abbey ruins run by Cadw, plus a small village with pubs and cafés. Check whether dogs are allowed in the abbey grounds.
A woodland climb up the "365 steps" to a viewpoint over the Wye's loops and the Severn. Steep; carriers only.
A cliff-top castle above the Wye, run by Cadw, with an old town gate and a riverside to wander. Visitors report dogs are allowed on the ground floor.
A dog-friendly tea room: brunch, lunch and cakes.

places.q: The Ugly Mug Cafe, Beaufort Square, Chepstow
places.note: An independent, family-run café with all-day breakfast and lunch. Dog-friendly.
An all-day café-bar, listed as dog-friendly, and open in the evenings.
A heritage steam railway. Dogs are allowed on the trains but not in the café or dining car. Check the half-term timetable.
places.near: 5 min from Taurus Crafts and Lydney Harbour

places.note: Craft studios, shops and a café in old farm buildings. Check the dog policy indoors.
A flat, open walk along the Severn estuary with big skies. Good when the forest is muddy. Windy, so wrap the babies up.

places.q: Silver Fox Cafe, Newnham on Severn
places.note: A riverside café that's dog-friendly, open for breakfast and lunch seven days a week. Newnham is a pretty village on the Severn.
places.near: North of Lydney on the A48

places.note: A market town under the Sugar Loaf with good food shops and a covered market.
Black-and-white timbered buildings and the cobbled Church Lane.
The book town. Lovely, but a long day with babies.

places.q: Drybridge Veterinary Clinic, Railway Drive, Coleford GL16 8RH
places.note: A vet in Coleford. Ring for hours and out-of-hours cover.

places.q: Severnside Veterinary Group, Cupola Close, Coleford GL16 8RD
places.note: A small-animal vet on the Mushet Industrial Park.
Opens a map search. Coleford has a Co-op and a Tesco (Lidl got planning permission in 2019, so check whether it's open). Monmouth and Ross have bigger shops.
Opens a map search for nearby chemists.

places.q: Forest of Dean Community Hospital, Cinderford
places.note: The local community hospital. Ring NHS 111 first to check where to go; 999 for emergencies.
places.geo: Forest of Dean Community Hospital, Cinderford

places.note: Opens a map search, for forgotten food, leads or poo bags.
The most recommended breakfast spot in Coleford: an independent café with home-cooked breakfasts, good veggie options, and indoor and outdoor seating. Listed as dog-friendly.

places.q: The Art of Coffee, Market Place, Coleford
places.note: Locally roasted coffee, plus breakfast, brunch and light lunches. Opens at 8am on weekdays.

places.q: Sixteen Community Cafe, Bank Street, Coleford
places.note: A not-for-profit café cooking with local ingredients. Open Monday to Saturday from 9am. Its dog policy isn't listed, so ask.

places.q: Victorias Coffee Shop, Broad Street, Ross-on-Wye
places.note: Brunch from 10am to 4pm. Known for its homemade sausage rolls, cakes and bakes. Dog-friendly.
A bright, independent coffee shop with an all-day menu, homemade cakes and outdoor seating. Listed as dog-friendly.

places.q: Ginger Nut Cafe, High Street, Ross-on-Wye
places.note: Breakfast and brunch, with good gluten-free options.

places.q: Forest Deli, 4 Market Place, Coleford GL16 8AQ
places.note: Local cheese (one of the best cheese counters in the area), honey, preserves, beer, cider and gin. Good for a night-in board.
A bakery that bakes on site. Reviewers praise its rye bread, sausage rolls and sourdough.

places.q: Wigmores Bakery, St Mary Street, Monmouth
places.note: An independent bakery for bread and cakes, from about 8am on weekdays.
Popular for baguettes and pastries.
A co-operative artisan bakery: long-fermentation bread and pastries made with locally milled organic flour. Check opening days before you go.
places.near: North-east side of the forest, on the way to Gloucester

places.q: Severn and Wye Smokery, Chaxhill, Westbury-on-Severn
places.note: A smokehouse with a food hall, fish counter, café and restaurant. Great for treat food for a night in. Check whether dogs are allowed inside.
A hilltop village with a small Norman castle (now a youth hostel, so you can only see it from outside) and views over the Wye. Walk down to the river from here.

walk.length: Village wander, or longer down to the Wye

places.note: A quiet riverside village. A flat stretch of the Wye Valley Walk runs from here towards Tintern, about 1.5 mi each way.

walk.length: About 3 mi there and back towards Tintern

places.note: A riverside village with an old railway bridge over the Wye and walks along the river towards Monmouth.
The biggest waterfalls in the area, at their best after rain. A short, steep woodland walk; carriers only.
A small, free, open castle ruin by the River Monnow in a pretty village. Quiet, with open grass.
Big, grand ruins run by Cadw. Check whether dogs are allowed.
A National Trust Dutch water garden. Quiet in October. Check the dog policy and opening days.
places.near: Next to the Severn & Wye Smokery

pairings: Symonds Yat: the Rock and the Biblins loop, then the Saracens Head, or 15 min on to Ross-on-Wye.
Staunton: the Buckstone, then the White Horse, or 10 min on to Monmouth.
Central forest: the Sculpture Trail, Beechenhurst Café, Cannop Ponds, and dinner at the Speech House.
Lakes: Mallards Pike, stopping at New Fancy View on the way, then the Wild Boar Coffee café at Parkend.
Lower Wye: the Devil's Pulpit at Tintern, then lunch and the castle in Chepstow (10 min).
Goodrich: Goodrich Castle, then lunch at the Inn on the Wye, then Ross.
Lydney side: Dean Forest Railway and Taurus Crafts, then a flat walk at Lydney Harbour.
Rainy day: Clearwell Caves (take turns, dogs stay on the surface) and Perrygrove Railway, 5–10 min apart.
Food run: Forest Deli and the Crusty Loaf in Coleford, or the Severn & Wye Smokery food hall for a night in.
tips: It's half-term. Book dinners early, and ask for a quiet corner table for the dog.
Clocks went back on 25 Oct. It's dark by about 4:45pm. Pack head torches if you walk to the New Inn.
Wear boots: leaves and mud make the paths slippery, especially carrying babies.
Keep the dog on a short lead in Wye Valley fields; sheep and cattle graze there, and the Forest has free-roaming sheep and wild boar.
Skip Puzzlewood: it allows no dogs and no pushchairs.
Places marked "Ring ahead" are from listings that weren't confirmed; check dogs are still welcome.
Phone signal is patchy in the forest. Open this page once on wifi and add it to your home screen; it then works offline (photos and maps need signal).
Emergencies: 999. Non-urgent medical: NHS 111. Vets and supplies are in the Essentials filter.

Baby: Sleeping bag and travel cot sheet
